# Configuration and State Management

This layer manages application configuration and state.

## Overview

It includes functions for parsing, analyzing, and managing code and comments.

## Key components

| File | Purpose | Main definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`src/apply.js`](../src/apply.js) | Applies changes and merges state, writing results. | `applyRun`, `docsLeft` |
| [`src/changes.js`](../src/changes.js) | Manages changes, docs, and git state. | `docExists`, `docsDone`, `findChanges`, `ignoreHash`, `needsComments`, `nothingToCover` |
| [`src/config.js`](../src/config.js) | Reads the action inputs from INPUT_* environment variables and validates them. | `COMMENT_LEVELS`, `EXISTING_CODE`, `ConfigError`, `readConfig`, `readInput`, `readList` |
| [`src/git.js`](../src/git.js) | Git operations for the Action. | `BaseBranchError`, `BOT_EMAIL`, `BOT_NAME`, `defaultBranch`, `IGNORE_FILE`, `UPDATE_BRANCH` |
| [`src/languages.js`](../src/languages.js) | The language table, plus the rules that decide whether a file is commented, only read for docs, or skipped. | `LANGUAGES`, `LEXER_TOKENS`, `LOCKFILES`, `MAX_FILE_BYTES`, `SKIP_DIRS`, `classifyFile` |
| [`src/links.js`](../src/links.js) | Generates links for generated text. | `cleanProseLine`, `forgetKnownUrls`, `hasUnknownUrl`, `keepCodeLine`, `knownUrls`, `normalizeUrl` |

| [`src/report.js`](../src/report.js) | Builds .docturnal/last-run.md, which the GitHub App uses as the pull request description. | `DOCS_TITLE`, `UPDATE_TITLE`, `buildReport`, `code`, `plainText`, `progressLines` |
| [`src/safe-path.js`](../src/safe-path.js) | Docturnal reads and writes a few paths by name: README.md, docs/, .docturnal/, and project files such as package.json. | `LinkError`, `isPlainPath`, `requirePlainPath` |
| [`src/state.js`](../src/state.js) | Reads and writes state files. | `LAST_RUN_PATH`, `STATE_PATH`, `emptyPending`, `emptyState`, `hashContent`, `readState` |

## How it works

For example, `config.js` reads the action inputs from INPUT_* environment variables and validates them. `state.js` reads and writes state files. `git.js` handles Git operations for the Action. `changes.js` manages changes, docs, and git state. `apply.js` applies changes and merges state, writing results. `links.js` generates links for generated text. `readme.js` manages the repository's README.md. `report.js` builds the .docturnal/last-run.md file, which the GitHub App uses as the pull request description.

## Configuration

- Environment variables: `BASE_BRANCH`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `PUSH`.
- Action inputs: `backlog-batch-size`, `comment-level`, `context-tokens`, `docs-dir`, `docs-model`, `exclude`, `existing-code`, `extensions`, `job-timeout-minutes`, `model`, `path`, `time-budget-minutes`.
- Configuration files: `.docturnal/readme.json`, `.docturnal/state.json`.
